readings.name: Pricing Power
readings.plain: Whether raising a fee brings in more revenue. It is Bullish only if the whole interval is above -1.

readings.name: NEAR's Share of Fees
readings.plain: The part of Intents fees that DefiLlama books as revenue. Bullish above 30%; Bearish only if it was under 20% on each of the last 14 days.

readings.name: Solver Competition
readings.plain: Two numbers: what solvers keep on $1,000 swaps, and how much of the volume the top 3 solvers fill. Bullish under 5 bps and 60%; Bearish over 10 bps or 80%.
readings.source: intents.near chain sample; not collected yet

readings.name: Largest Integrator
readings.plain: The largest frontend's share of the fees paid over the last 30 days. Bullish under 50%; Bearish over 80%.

readings.name: Path to Deflation
readings.detail: 90-day revenue rose over the last 3 months
readings.plain: Whether the 90-day revenue total rose (or fell) at each of the last three month-ends.

labelCheck.rule: Labels with confidence 'secondary' dropped; the readings use referral names, so sides and shares stay the same

fixed: Tideline asks whether NEAR Intents fees could ever cover the new NEAR being issued. This is research, not financial advice.
A Bullish reading means the evidence passed a line set in advance, not that the price will rise.
live: As of 5 Nov, too little is measured to lean either way.
Pointing Bullish: NEAR's share of fees is 33% over the last 30 days and revenue has risen over each of the last three months. The DefiLlama figures come from a dataset nobody can re-run for free.
Not measured yet: Pricing Power, Solver Competition and Largest Integrator.

Monthly volume would need to reach about 3.4x today's level under the 1.6% issuance plan, which passed its vote but is not in force yet, or 5.4x if issuance stays at 2.5%, with all revenue spent on buybacks.
